genZNote: The 'owl's eye' inclusion body under the microscope is basically the virus signing its own name in the tissue.

morphology.shape: Enveloped icosahedral virion with a large dsDNA genome

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human host cells, particularly epithelial cells, monocytes, and their precursors, where it establishes lifelong latency
habitat.hostAssociation: Establishes latency in monocytes/myeloid progenitor cells after primary infection, with potential for reactivation during immunosuppression
habitat.reservoir: Latently infected humans; extremely widespread, with most adults seropositive by middle age

identificationClues: 'Owl's eye' intranuclear inclusion bodies on histopathology — a classic diagnostic clue in infected tissue
Diagnosed by PCR viral load, pp65 antigenemia assay, or serology depending on clinical context
Leading infectious cause of congenital sensorineural hearing loss and neurologic disability when transmitted in utero
Reactivates in immunocompromised hosts (transplant recipients, advanced HIV/AIDS), causing retinitis, colitis, pneumonitis, or other end-organ disease

diseases: Usually asymptomatic or a mononucleosis-like illness in immunocompetent hosts
Congenital CMV infection — the leading infectious cause of congenital sensorineural hearing loss and can cause microcephaly and intellectual disability
CMV retinitis, colitis, esophagitis, and pneumonitis in immunocompromised patients (AIDS, transplant recipients)
virulenceFactors: Establishment of lifelong latency in myeloid cells, evading immune clearance
Ability to modulate MHC class I expression, impairing cytotoxic T-cell recognition of infected cells
clinicalImportance.transmission: Contact with infected body fluids (saliva, urine, blood, breast milk, genital secretions); vertical (congenital) transmission in utero; transplant/transfusion-associated transmission
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common congenital infections worldwide and a major cause of preventable childhood hearing loss; a leading opportunistic pathogen in solid organ and stem cell transplant recipients and in advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4 <50 cells/µL for CMV retinitis)
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Quantitative PCR viral load is used both for diagnosis and for monitoring response to antiviral therapy in immunocompromised patients, particularly post-transplant

examFacts.importantDisease: Congenital CMV (leading infectious cause of congenital hearing loss); CMV retinitis/colitis in immunocompromised hosts
examFacts.importantTest: Quantitative PCR viral load; pp65 antigenemia; histopathology showing owl's eye inclusions
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A herpesvirus producing 'owl's eye' intranuclear inclusions, the leading infectious cause of congenital hearing loss, and a classic reactivation pathogen in transplant/AIDS patients
